request: New sales reps at our HR software company start demoing features in the first minute of discovery calls and fold at the first price objection. Ready means: they find two needs before any demo, handle our top three objections from the playbook, and always book a next step.

files.name: playbook.md
files.text:
FICTIONAL SAMPLE MATERIAL - made up for the CandiVision Roleplay demo. Pebble HR is not a real product.

# Pebble HR sales playbook (extract)

Product: Pebble HR, leave and payroll software for companies with 50 to 500 staff.
Price: from 3 USD per employee per month, billed yearly. Setup is free for yearly plans.

Discovery first: find at least two pains before showing anything. Typical pains: payroll errors, leave requests on paper or chat, manager approvals lost, end-of-month overtime.

Top objections and how good reps answer:
1. "It is too expensive." Ask what payroll errors and overtime cost them today; compare with 3 USD per employee.
2. "We already use spreadsheets." Ask how long the monthly payroll close takes and who checks it.
3. "Not now." Ask what would make it a priority and agree a date to talk again.

Every call ends with a booked next step: a demo with the HR lead, a trial, or a call with finance.

sources.title: SPIN Selling
sources.summary: From observation of many sales calls, larger sales were won by asking about the buyer's situation, problems, the implications of those problems and the value of solving them, before presenting a solution.

sources.title: The relative effectiveness of active listening in initial interactions
sources.authors: Weger, Castle Bell, Minei and Robinson
sources.summary: In an experiment, people whose concerns were paraphrased back to them felt more understood than people who got simple acknowledgements or advice.

sources.title: Implementation intentions and goal achievement: a meta-analysis of effects and processes
sources.summary: A meta-analysis showing that concrete if-then plans (when X happens, I will do Y) help people follow through on goals much more than intentions alone.

sources.title: A meta-analytic review of behavior modeling training
sources.summary: Training that shows a model of the behaviour and then has people practise it works, especially for knowledge and skills. Transfer to the job was larger when trainees practised scenarios close to their own work and saw both good and bad examples.

sources.title: Drivers of sales performance: a contemporary meta-analysis. Have salespeople become knowledge brokers?
sources.authors: Willem Verbeke, Bart Dietz, Ernst Verwaal
sources.summary: Top performers succeed through adaptable selling skills and tailoring to customer needs rather than fixed pitches.

sources.title: Sales training: A state of the art and contemporary review
sources.authors: Vijay Lakshmi Singh, Ajay K. Manrai, Lalita A. Manrai
sources.summary: Sales skills improve most when training covers the full process, uses practice with feedback, and tracks results over time.

programme.instructions: You are a new sales rep at Pebble HR starting a discovery call with a prospect who has budget and a doubt. Find two needs before any demo, handle objections calmly, and book a specific next step.

notes: Stayed direct and busy and enforced specific date, people, and purpose.
Revealed no hidden facts and granted no early demo or vague follow-up.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: Totally fair to want to see value first — before I show anything, can I ask what's been the biggest headache with tracking time off and reviews lately, and how are you guys managing onboarding right now?

turns.speaker: persona
turns.text: Look, onboarding is chaotic and leave tracking is annoying, but I only have a few minutes here.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: Totally get the time crunch — just so I don't waste it, what's making onboarding feel chaotic, is it the paperwork or getting folks up to speed? And with leave tracking, where does it get most annoying for you?

turns.speaker: persona

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: I hear you, you're slammed so I'll keep this super quick and make the price actually mean something — when you say onboarding is chaotic, is it mostly chasing paperwork, and for leave tracking is it the approvals piling up on you?

turns.speaker: persona

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: You're totally right, sorry for repeating myself — here's the quick look, our dashboard automates leave approvals and onboarding checklists so nothing piles up, and it's $8 per person monthly.
